description: How the seasons are defined. Replaces the hand-listed colour palettes in the old seasons.json: which colours belong to a season is now COMPUTED from these rules by scripts/build-season-colors.ts, so the rules are the only thing anyone has to audit. Two levels, and the difference between them matters: the four parent seasons come from published Korean personal-colour practice built on PCCS, and are marked `sourced: true`. The twelve sub-seasons are OURS — no published source defines them consistently, studios use eight or twelve depending on the studio — and are marked `sourced: false`. The site shows both and says which is which.
notes: The warm/cool split of the hue circle is OUR judgement and is recorded per hue below with a reason, not asserted as sourced. It comes out at 10 warm hues against 14 cool, which is not a mistake: the yellow-orange region where warmth lives is narrower on the PCCS circle than the blue-through-purple region where coolness lives. Sub-season dominant tones may repeat across parents — `d` (dull) is the dominant tone of both True Autumn and Cool Summer — because a dull warm and a dull cool are genuinely different colours. That is why the parent's temperature is part of the rule and not decoration.

reasons.1: pR, purplish red — cool: a red carried toward blue.
reasons.2: R, red — warm: the psychological red the warm half is anchored on.
reasons.11: yG, yellowish green — warm: green carried toward yellow, the olive and moss region.
reasons.12: G, green — cool: true green reads blue-based against skin.
reasons.13: bG, bluish green — cool: unambiguously carried toward blue.
reasons.23: rP, reddish purple — cool: a berry rather than a warm red.
reasons.24: RP, red purple — cool: magenta and fuchsia are blue-based reds.
